claim: The items from all eight Croatian sources were searched for data or findings on EU workers' access to jobs in Croatia, or their treatment there, after accession, and none exists. The only applied step after accession is the 2015 reciprocal permit statement.
problem: Contradicted by the case's own evidence. The 2015 item is itself a post-accession finding on the treatment of EU nationals (permits required from nationals of restricting Member States). The 2023 government bill also records that the Ombudswoman had pointed to the inconsistency of the Civil Servants Act citizenship condition with EU free movement law, and that the legislation is being aligned for that reason; the Act then opened civil service posts to EEA nationals from 1 January 2024. So a nationality barrier to EU workers' access was reported a decade after the 2012 'completed alignment' finding. Calling these RI-FMW-003 context does not make the blanket 'none exists' true, and the conflict with the 2012 rating is not reported as CLAUDE.md requires.
suggested_fix: Narrow the claim to: no data on EU workers' take-up or experience in the labour market generally. State the 2015 permit finding and the 2023 Ombudswoman and bill statements as the only post-accession material, both legal in kind. Record that a 2023 government text treats a citizenship condition as misaligned after the 2012 completed alignment rating, cited with the public sector scope limit.

claim: The source does not say whether the 2011 amendments it mentions under Chapter 23 are NN 130/2011. The Act took effect in two steps... The Commission said Croatia largely fulfilled the requirements on access to the labour market in 2011.
problem: Chronology settles what the case leaves open. The 2011 Progress Report is dated 12 October 2011 (source register); NN 130/2011 was passed on 28 October 2011 and printed on 16 November 2011. Amendments the report describes as adopted cannot be that Act, and NN 130/2011 is a new Act that repeals NN 79/07 and 36/09 and is not an amending act. The 2011 'largely fulfils' rating also predates the Act, yet it sits in the how_implemented account of the Act and HRV-EU-2011-001-0003 is listed under its reform items. The item also gives no year, so 'the 2011 amendments' is unsupported.
suggested_fix: Say that the 2011 rating and the amendments it mentions predate NN 130/2011 and refer to an earlier unidentified text. Move both out of the Act's implementation account, take HRV-EU-2011-001-0003 out of its reform chain, and correct INT-HRV-0006 by a proposed new reason. Give the date gap as the reason in cannot_be_attributed for the 2011 rating.

claim: No outcome evidence found... none exists. The government permit count does not show the law being applied. Only secondary-act timing and the permit count are given as post-adoption facts.
problem: MNE-GOV-2026-003 page 86 states, in the migration section, that implementation of the amending law (SL 3/26) continued in the reporting period, and that applying the new legal solutions further improved procedures, including the exercise of the rights of EU nationals and their family members in line with EU standards. This text is in the source but was not extracted, so no item carries it. The search of items is literally true, but the case and the status reason read as if no source speaks to application. It is unverified government self-reporting and is no proof of success, yet it bears directly on implementation status and on the Article 221b deferral, because it sits uneasily with clauses that apply only from accession.
evidence_item_ids: MNE-GOV-2026-003-0006;MNE-GOV-2026-001-0005 (the passage itself is not an item: sources/MNE/GOV/text/MNE-GOV-2026-003.txt page 86)
suggested_fix: Extract the passage as an item (machine translated, government self-report), cite it in the case as an uncorroborated stated claim, and re-propose the INT-MNE-0002 reason with it. Also widen the absence wording to say what was searched: items or full source text.

claim: The Commission reports work permits issued under the foreigners legislation in 2023 and 2024, so the general permit regime is in use.
problem: The value does not follow. The cited items give counts and do not name the legislation they were issued under. The same counts are treated differently elsewhere in this package: the CMP-0003 evidence field says no source links them to a reform, INT-SRB-0001 says 'No source gives usage or processing data, so in_practice is not supported' although the 2024 count falls after its 1 February 2024 application date, and INT-MNE-0002 says a permit count does not show the law being applied. The value is also the highest status in a stalled case and concerns a law whose EU clause is not in force, and the 2024 count may fall under the amended regime rather than the 2014 text.
suggested_fix: Propose implemented or insufficient_evidence, and apply one rule to permit counts across INT-SRB-0001, INT-SRB-0006 and INT-MNE-0002. If in_practice stays, split the record so the EU clause has its own status of adopted, by Serbia's account, and not yet applicable.

claim: The underlying mechanism is a legal one: write equal treatment... and tie commencement to accession. The drafting mechanism is transferable in principle: a separate regime... with named clauses tied to accession.
problem: Goes further than the evidence. Each case's own cannot_be_attributed text says the evidence cannot show deferred commencement was accepted or necessary. The third case points the other way: Serbia reported a free-access clause commencing on accession in the 2014 law, and in the same report the Commission found the legislation not yet in line. In 2024 and 2025 it still found partial alignment. This counter-example is not raised in either transferable field, and Serbia's case only says it cannot show whether a deferred clause is enough. There is no transferability judgement to carry the conditions, and in Montenegro the timing of the equal-treatment clause itself is unknown.
suggested_fix: Separate the two elements. Equal treatment and permit-free work in the law can be stated as what the acquis requires. Present commencement on accession as an untested design choice, noting that Croatia's rating is unattributed, Montenegro's is untested and Serbia's reported clause coexisted with findings of misalignment. Add the cross-case point to all three cases.

claim: Croatia carried the reform in one Aliens Act. The reform sat in one Aliens Act.
problem: Unsupported and at odds with the case. Limitations say the Commission never says which law closed the gap; the Commission asked for 'a series of amendments'; a separate Employment Mediation Act amendment was planned in 2007 with status unknown; and the 2011 amendments are unidentified.
suggested_fix: Say: the EU worker provisions read here sit in one Aliens Act; whether other laws were also changed is not known.

claim: The Commission found that important adjustments were needed. In 2015 the Commission found Serbian law not yet in line with the acquis.
problem: Selective. Each 'adjustments' sentence begins 'However' and follows an extracted Commission finding that the country had 'reached a satisfactory level of alignment' in the chapter overall. Both are omitted, so the starting gap reads wider than the report's own overall finding.
suggested_fix: Add the overall finding alongside the access to the labour market finding in both cases.

claim: The Commission's 2007 wording on non-discrimination and permits for EU workers.
problem: HRV-EU-2007-001-0004 is cited, but it is flagged reported_view and sits in Part II, the country's own account, so it is not Commission wording.
suggested_fix: Attribute that item to Croatia or remove it; the two Commission items carry the claim.

claim: Sources agree on adoption.
problem: Only one source is cited, the Act itself. The Commission items do not name it, so there is no agreement of sources to rely on for tier 2 treatment.
suggested_fix: Say: adoption rests on the Official Gazette text alone.

claim: No usable item states its position at the context date. No later item states whether it continues at the context date.
problem: An extracted item says the arrangements end irrevocably on 30 June 2020, and the intervention record itself repeats this. Article 236 limits the measure to the duration of Member States' measures. The stated end date is available and bears on both records, yet neither reason gives it. The exclusion follows the G5b condition but is not disclosed as a known end date.
suggested_fix: State in both reasons that a treaty end date of 30 June 2020 is recorded in a queued item not used under G5b, and raise at G6b whether that item should be released for this purpose.

claim: Croatia wrote equal treatment... into its 2011 Aliens Act, commencing on accession, and the Commission recorded completed legal alignment in 2012.
problem: The one-line summary joins reform and rating with 'and', with no note that no source connects them. The summary is the field most likely to be reused, and it invites the reading the case body rejects.
suggested_fix: Add: no source links the two.

claim: Commission alignment ratings, chapter closure and permit counts are filed as implementation.
problem: Reform, implementation and outcome are blurred in the item lists. The 2011 and 2012 alignment ratings, the Montenegro provisional closure with the EU return clause, and Serbian partial alignment ratings are EU assessments or negotiating steps and are not implementation of the reform. Permit counts are use data. The text labels them correctly, but the structured fields do not.
suggested_fix: Add a separate list for assessments and negotiating steps, or a note on the field saying that these items are context.

claim: The Act is machine translated (capped at Medium).
problem: LIM-0029 allows machine-translated legal texts where no English version exists. An English text of the Aliens Act does exist (HRV-GOV-2013-001 is its free excerpt, and the rest is on sale). Not buying it is proper, but the use falls outside the wording of the limit and this is not disclosed.
suggested_fix: Note this in the limitations and ask Sofia to confirm or extend LIM-0029 at G6b to cover English versions that are not freely available.

claim: The EU reports that Chapter 2 was provisionally closed on 15 June 2026.
problem: The EU release gives no 15 June date in its text or in the item, and it was published on 16 June per the register. The date comes only from the machine-translated government annex, which conflicts with itself on the venue.
suggested_fix: Attribute closure to the EU release and the date to the government annex.

claim: Whether Article 178a applies now or from accession depends on Article 221 of the base law, which was not read. The timing of Article 178a is unknown because Article 221 of the base law was not read.
problem: No item or read source says that Article 221 governs this. The amending law refers only to inserting Article 221b after Article 221a. Since the base law was not read, the reference to Article 221 has no traceable basis in the evidence and appears to come from outside it. The uncertainty is real, but the legal reference is unsupported.
suggested_fix: Say: the amending law does not say when Article 178a applies, and the base law's commencement clauses were not read. Name Article 221 only with a source.

claim: The law is machine translated (capped at Medium).
problem: The limitation omits that the government annex is also machine translated, although the closing benchmark statement and the 638 count rest on it. LIM-0029 covers legal texts only and LIM-0012 covers Macedonian and Albanian only, so no logged limit covers a machine-translated Montenegrin government report.
suggested_fix: State that the annex is machine translated and capped at Medium, and propose an extension of LIM-0029 at G6b.

claim: (No statement on later amendments to the Law on Foreigners.)
problem: The annex cites the Law on Foreigners as SL 12/2018, 3/2019, 86/2022, 77/2024, 3/2026 and 33/2026 (page 67), so there is a further 2026 amendment, and page 139 reports a Blue Card bill under access to the labour market. The case does not mention either, unlike CMP-0001, which discloses unchecked later amendments. The 33/2026 text may bear on the EU regime or Article 221b. The Blue Card text concerns third-country workers, so it is likely to be context.
evidence_item_ids: MNE-GOV-2026-003-0006 (passages are not items: sources/MNE/GOV/text/MNE-GOV-2026-003.txt pages 67 and 139)
suggested_fix: Disclose that SL 33/2026 was not read, and check it if it is public.

claim: North Macedonia has the same stated barrier in its foreigners law, and is told to exclude EU citizens from annual quotas... a requirement stated for North Macedonia in nearly the same terms.
problem: This omits a known conflict. North Macedonia's own account says that quotas do not apply to EU citizens following a reciprocity agreement, while the Commission asks for their exclusion. The validated gap judgement JDG-009552 reports this conflict. The case carries only one side of it, and the High rating leans on the quota match.
suggested_fix: State the conflict in the lesson and in the relevance reason, citing both sides.

claim: Same issue and mechanism... an equal-treatment clause and a quota carve-out in the foreigners law.
problem: The quota carve-out is an RI-FMW-002 element by the case's own label, and MKD-EU-2025-003-0028 is a defining item of RI-FMW-002 in the taxonomy. The only RI-FMW-001 element is Article 178a, whose timing is unknown. A High for RI-FMW-001 therefore rests partly on a neighbouring issue, and this is not said.
suggested_fix: Rest the reason on Article 178a and MKD-EU-2025-003-0033, and mention the quota as a neighbouring match. Reconsider High or Medium at G6b.

claim: The evidence gives no comparable measure of size.
problem: Contradicted in part. Annual permit quotas of 28 988 (Montenegro) and 10 000 (North Macedonia) are a comparable measure of scale. Permit shares for EU citizens exist for Serbia (3% in 2024) and North Macedonia (12.8% in 2020 and 10.7% in 2021, by its own account). The years differ and the measures are rough, but they exist.
suggested_fix: Say: only rough measures exist, namely permit quotas and EU shares in different years. Cite them.

claim: Amendments in 2017 and 2018, and in July 2023, simplified permit procedures for foreigners generally.
problem: For 2017 and 2018 the only source says the law was amended 'in order to further simplify' procedures, which is an aim and not an achieved effect. INT-SRB-0002 words this correctly, but the case does not. The years are read from Gazette numbers in a single clause of a posted workers study.
suggested_fix: Say: 2017 and 2018 amendments made, according to a secondary study, in order to simplify procedures. Keep 'simplified' for 2023 only, attributed to the Commission.

claim: The evidence shows no reform since 2014 aimed at the treatment of EU workers. The reforms in the evidence since 2014 simplify permits for all foreigners and do not address the issue.
problem: Stronger than the evidence allows. The base law is inaccessible, the 31/19 amendment listed in the register was not read, and the content of 113/17 and 50/18 is known from one clause. The same paragraph of that study also says laws on foreigners were revised in all four countries, including Serbia, to include 'the posting of EU workers'; this was not extracted. Posting is narrow, and the Commission's findings still support the stalled reading, but 'for foreigners generally' and 'do not address' are not established.
evidence_item_ids: SRB-RES-2021-001-0001;SRB-EU-2024-001-0004;SRB-EU-2025-001-0005 (posting sentence is not an item: sources/SRB/RES/text/SRB-RES-2021-001.txt page 15)
suggested_fix: Say: no reform aimed at EU workers' access is visible in what was read, while the content of the 2017, 2018 and 2019 amendments is largely unread and a secondary study mentions posting of EU workers. Add the 2019 amendment to the limitations.

claim: Amending the foreigners law to simplify permits for all foreigners can earn a chapter-level finding of limited progress from the Commission while the gap it names remains.
problem: Overstated. Each limited progress finding has two stated grounds: in 2024, also preparations to join EURES; in 2025, also improving electronic data exchange with Member States. The permit reform is one ground of two, and the case does not say so.
suggested_fix: Say: permit simplification was one of two grounds for the Commission's limited progress finding in each year.

claim: Serbia is a stalled case with the same gap in nearly the same words.
problem: The wording differs: Serbia is 'covered by rules for third-country nationals', and North Macedonia 'does not distinguish between EU citizens and other foreigners'. The substance is close but not the same gap, since the validated North Macedonia gap includes reserved private sector posts, which no Serbian item addresses. The partial alignment wording does match.
suggested_fix: Say: a closely similar finding in different words, covering the permit regime but not reserved private sector posts.

claim: Serbia reported a clause giving EU citizens free access on accession in 2014.
problem: Date is imprecise and conflicts with the case body. The law was adopted in 2014, and Serbia's account appears in the 2015 screening report. The source does not date the report by Serbia to 2014.
suggested_fix: Say: Serbia reported in the 2015 screening report that its 2014 law contains a clause giving free access on accession.
